headline: The supported Node.js floor is 24.22.1, which fixes the out-of-bounds write in the bundled Brotli decoder (CVE-2026-111497)
summary:
Node.js 24.22.1, 26.12.1 and 22.23.4 fix CVE-2026-111497, an out-of-bounds write in the Brotli decoder Node bundles. A crafted Brotli stream can crash the process, disclose memory, or run code. `engines.node` is now `>=24.22.1`. On Node 26, use 26.12.1 or later.

The framework reaches that decoder through TLS certificate compression. On every TLS 1.3 connection it opens, and on listeners that request client certificates, it offers the certificate-compression algorithms Node reports, which include Brotli, so a peer can send a Brotli-compressed certificate that Node decodes during the handshake, before the certificate is verified. `b.safeDecompress` with `algorithm: "brotli"` also passes its input to the decoder. On Node 24.22.1 or 26.12.1 neither path reaches the flaw. `engines` is not enforced at runtime, so upgrade Node itself; installing this release does not patch an older runtime.

items.title: Run on Node.js 24.22.1 or 26.12.1
items.body: CVE-2026-111497 is an out-of-bounds write in the Brotli decoder that Node.js compiles in. Every Node.js release before 22.23.4, 24.22.1 and 26.12.1 is affected, including Node 26.0 through 26.12.0, which the `>=24.22.1` range still admits. On an affected runtime, a TLS peer can send a Brotli-compressed certificate that Node decodes during the handshake, before any certificate check, and `b.safeDecompress` with `algorithm: "brotli"` decodes whatever input it is given. Upgrade the runtime and rebuild any image that embeds it.

items.title: `b.watcher` starts on a tree that holds an unreadable directory
items.body: On Linux, Node 24.22.1 and 26.12.1 refuse a recursive `fs.watch` with `EACCES` when any directory under the root cannot be read, where Node 24.21.0 skipped such a directory. `b.watcher.create` in `fs` mode then threw `watcher/start-failed`. When the root is readable and `fs.watch` refuses with `EACCES` or `EPERM`, the watcher now polls the tree instead, skipping directories it cannot read: the handle's `mode` is `"poll"`, and `onError` receives a `watcher/recursive-unreadable` notice that names the refused directory.

items.title: Vendored `@blamejs/pki` 0.9.9
items.body: `@blamejs/pki` moves from 0.9.7 to 0.9.9. It requires Node 24.22.1. It refuses an IPv4 address spelled as a host name, such as `0127.0.0.1` or `0x7f.0.0.1`, wherever it matches a certificate identity, validates a path for an identity, or dials as a TLS server name, instead of comparing it with dNSName entries. A zstd input to its certificate decompression must be exactly one Zstandard frame.

items.title: `engines.node` is `>=24.22.1`
items.body: The framework and the wiki example declare `>=24.22.1`, and CI, the npm publish workflow and the container workflow run Node 24.22.1. The wiki example's default base images, used by a local `docker build` without build arguments, move to Chainguard `node` digests that carry Node 26.12.1; the release workflow already resolves current digests when it builds.
